study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Jing et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneous brain dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug-naive patients with major depressive disorder

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and methods clearly state the objective to use normative modeling to characterize individual-level deviations and identify subtypes of first-episode drug-naive MDD based on dynamic functional connectivity, which specifies both research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "...we investigated subtypes of patients with first-episode drug-naive (FEDN) depression... A multivariate unsupervised normative modeling method was used to identify subtypes of FEDN and their associated networks, focusing on individual-level variability..."; "To elucidate MDD heterogeneity and identify robust MDD subtypes... we adopted the normative modeling method..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For the newly built normative model, the study describes eligibility criteria for healthy controls (age 18–50; motion thresholds), cites the original dataset publication for preprocessing, specifies quality criteria (FD thresholds), reports final sample sizes, and describes matching to patients from the same center to avoid site effects.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "...subjects with age in the range of 18 to 50; (3) subjects with less head motion (mean FD <= 0.5 mm or max FD <= 2 mm). To avoid the center effect, 164 healthy individuals and 91 FEDN-MDD patients (60 females) from the same center were included."; "we used the matchIt function... to select the comparable group from the healthy controls as the healthy-base group..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is explicitly modeled in the normative model, and site effects are addressed by restricting patients and healthy-base controls to the same center; matching also considered sex and education. However, sex is not explicitly included as a covariate in the normative model itself, and no harmonization method beyond sampling/matching is described.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...second-order polynomial regression normative model... on the relationship between age and these 40 features..."; "To avoid the center effect, 164 healthy individuals and 91 FEDN-MDD patients... from the same center were included."; "...matchIt... to select the comparable group... on... sex, age, and educational levels."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort source is specified as the International Big-Data Center for Depression Research (IBCDR), with website and citations to prior publications.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "...data from International Big-Data Center for Depression Research (IBCDR)... (The data is available by request... Website: http://yanlab.psych.ac.cn/IBCDR)..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from an existing dataset were used; per guidance, answer NA when secondary data are used for the reference cohort.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: resting-state fMRI was preprocessed using DPARSF with a standardized protocol, and quality control included motion thresholds.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "...preprocessed using the DPARSF software with a standardized protocol... subjects with less head motion (mean FD <= 0.5 mm or max FD <= 2 mm)."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They applied 10-fold cross-validation to assess generalization and built an aggregated normative model per feature, which tests the model on samples not used for fitting in each fold.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To assess generalization, we applied 10-fold cross-validation to build an aggregation normative model for each feature..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals is described. An independent healthy sample was used only to derive group-level ICA components (guidance), not for external validation of the normative model.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Another independent sample... was a healthy-ICA group to create the group-level components as guidance information in ICA."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The normative modeling approach is detailed: second-order polynomial regression relating features to age, estimation of the 50th percentile with bootstrapped CIs, scaling by 5th–95th percentiles to yield normalized z-scores, and 10-fold cross-validation aggregation.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "...second-order polynomial regression normative model... on the relationship between age and these 40 features... We estimated the 50th (median) percentile with bootstrapping confidence intervals... used the range between the 5th and 95th percentiles... to normalize the z-scores..."; "To assess generalization, we applied 10-fold cross-validation..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative fit or calibration metrics for the normative model (e.g., R^2, prediction error, or coverage). It only provides a qualitative statement in the Discussion that most participants fit the normative model well.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "...most participants fit the normative model well, suggesting that most were in the normal range of variation."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation was used, the study does not report sample sizes or demographic characteristics for each partition (fold).
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "To assess generalization, we applied 10-fold cross-validation..." (no further details on partition characteristics).

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Some information supports reproducibility: data source and access conditions (IBCDR by request) are provided; preprocessing software is named (DPARSF); and one package/version is cited (R MatchIt 4.4.0). However, software/library versions for core analyses and code/model availability are not provided.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "The data is available by request... Website: http://yanlab.psych.ac.cn/IBCDR"; "preprocessed using the DPARSF software with a standardized protocol"; "matchIt function in R... versions/4.4.0..."
